title: Superflow vs BugHerd
kicker: · SUPERFLOW VS BUGHERD · THE AI QA REVIEWER FOR AGENCIES
headline: BugHerd is a QA tool. Superflow is a QA tool + a team.
secondary: The team is AI agents, built from your QA checklist. They check every site change and pin what they find. Your team decides. Your client approves from a link.
prevents: Stop finding every mistake by hand.
No more manual pass before launch.
qualifier: If your agency reviews client sites in BugHerd, this page is for you.
heroCaption: It's like BugHerd hired a QA team.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: BugHerd was built before AI could check a site.
leftFacts: Agents run your checklist. Every change, desktop and mobile.
Findings land as pinned comments, rationale attached.
rightFacts: A person clicks through the pages and pins what they catch.
dimensions.verdict: A board is a record of what a person already caught. That's the part Superflow removes.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Feedback is easy to collect. A yes is harder.
leftFacts: Multi-step review flows: agents check, your team gates, then the client.
Your client opens a link and taps Approve. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.
rightFacts: Guests comment from a link, real and free.
Statuses track the work. A formal approval flow: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: BugHerd's guest link is good. The difference is the gate: in Superflow, the client's yes is a recorded step, not a comment.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: Half of client work lives behind a password.
leftFacts: Superflow lives on the site itself: passwords, Okta, SSO, no extension needed, guests included.
rightFacts: Reviews the live site, same as Superflow: even, and it says so.
Behind logins and SSO: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Both review the live site. Behind logins, the BugHerd side is pending verification; if it resolves even, it renders even.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal-only notes your team sees and the client never does.
The debate stays private; the client sees one settled answer.
dimensions.verdict: Renders as a difference only if the BugHerd side resolves to one.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both tools pin. The difference is what gets attached without asking.
leftFacts: Element and text pins, area comments.
A screenshot attaches to every comment automatically.
Recordings: screen, video, voice, from the toolbar.
rightFacts: Element pins with browser, OS, and screen size attached, genuinely good metadata.
Automatic per-comment screenshots: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Pinning is even. Capture is the gap: proof attaches itself in Superflow.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Boards hold tasks. They don't accumulate a client.
leftFacts: Brand rules and past decisions, learned once, fed to the agents next project.
rightFacts: No such concept in product. Each project starts blank.
dimensions.verdict: The tenth project should not start like the first.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The fix still has to ship.
leftFacts: Two-way Asana, Monday, ClickUp. Slack built in.
rightFacts: Jira, Trello, Asana, ClickUp, Slack, Teams in the list.
dimensions.verdict: BugHerd syncs Jira and Trello. We don't. If Jira is your spine, weigh that honestly.

pricingCompetitor: Verified July 2026: Standard $50, Studio $80, Premium $150 per month. +$8 per extra member. Enterprise custom with SSO. Guests free.
switchingLines: One snippet on any site; one click on Webflow, WordPress, or GTM.
Paste the checklist you already have; agents assemble from it.
Open BugHerd projects finish in BugHerd. Nothing migrates on day one.
honestCloseStrengths: BugHerd earned its place. Pins land on the element with the browser and OS attached. The kanban is built in. Clients comment free from a link. The integration list runs deep.
stayLine: If a careful human pass works for your studio, BugHerd is a fine tool. Stay.

faq.question: Is Superflow just BugHerd with AI on top?
faq.answer: No. BugHerd files what a person found; Superflow's agents do the finding. A person makes every call.

faq.question: Do the agents replace my reviewers?
faq.answer: No. Agents run the first pass. Your team, then your client, signs off.

faq.question: What happens to our BugHerd projects?
faq.answer: Finish them in BugHerd. Start new work in Superflow. Nothing migrates on day one.

faq.question: Will our clients have to learn a new tool?
faq.answer: No. They get a link and an Approve button. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.

faq.question: We push tasks to Jira from BugHerd.
faq.answer: Superflow syncs two-way with Asana, Monday, and ClickUp, plus webhooks and a REST API. Jira is not built in today; if Jira runs your delivery, weigh that.
